title: Structured logging — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, an incident reviewer asks what a log event contains. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud what one log event contains, and name a field you deliberately left out.

vocabulary.meaning: recording enough to diagnose an incident while carrying nothing that would harm if the log were read by anyone
a value deliberately kept out of a log line, named in the design so that it is not reintroduced later

expectedElements: The event fields are enumerated concretely
One deliberately excluded field is named
The diagnostic value of the remaining fields is defended
modelAnswer: A log event carries the timestamp, the correlation identifier, the operation name, the outcome, the duration, and the identifier of the affected record. What it deliberately does not carry is the request body, and I want to name that explicitly so nobody adds it back later thinking it was an oversight. The reason is that the body contains customer data, and a log is read by more people than the database is. The remaining fields are still enough as diagnostic evidence: with the correlation identifier and the record identifier I can reconstruct what happened without seeing the payload. Is there a diagnosis you have needed the body for?
commonMistakes: Describing logging as safe without naming a single excluded field
Excluding fields so aggressively that no incident can be reconstructed
variants: Answer again to a reviewer who asks for the payload during an incident.
